capabilities: Edit inline and block LaTeX formulas visually in the note or in a dedicated editor window
Scan formulas from the screen, clipboard, photos, note images or handwriting into LaTeX
Search a formula library by name, description or partial LaTeX and insert the result
Convert PDF pages into Markdown notes with editable LaTeX formulas
Expand shorthands into LaTeX and rewrite formulas with AI instructions
extras: Freemium: the visual editor, shorthands and formula search are free; cloud scanning, drawing, Magic edit and PDF conversion use credits (3 trial, 10 free, 5/month top-up) and an account after the trial, with paid plans for unlimited use. Self-hosted scanning via LaTeX-OCR is free. Includes detailed privacy disclosures about network use, clipboard, camera, microphone and screen capture.
intentEvidence: MathLive by Arno Gourdol, the math editor this plugin is built on
problem: Obsidian only offers typed LaTeX source for math, with no visual editing and no way to capture formulas from PDFs, screenshots, photos or handwriting.

relations.evidence: MathLive by Arno Gourdol, the math editor this plugin is built on
LaTeX-OCR by Lukas Blecher, for self-hosted scanning
when Latex Suite (or Quick Latex) is on, MathLive leaves typed LaTeX between $ signs to it
Imports your Quick Latex shortcuts and works alongside Latex Suite
The library comes from Wikidata's formulas

requires.name: MathLive API key (alternative to account sign-in)

summary: Visual LaTeX math editor that turns formulas in notes into editable widgets and scans formulas from screenshots, PDFs, photos and handwriting.
